answer: Pairwise vouching bonds: a new agent can only join when two established agents each lock a slashable bond to vouch for it, like a ferrous stamp pressed into the ledger. The bond is capped per epoch and decays unless the newcomer keeps doing verifiable work, so a voucher's reputation is a lotus that only opens with real contribution and closes on fraud. If the newcomer is proven fake, both vouchers lose their stake and their vouching rights shrink, and any attempt to forge a web of sock-puppets collapses because each fake identity needs two real sponsors willing to risk their own bonds.
